newsitem.title: USA: CME meat futures may rise despite high pork stocks.
newsitem.headline: CME meat futures may rise despite high pork stocks.

text.p: Tuesday's USDA U.S. Cold Storage report was considered mostly neutral to bullish to CME livestock pits, with pork bellies seen benefiting most despite rising total pork stocks, analysts said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department reported total frozen pork stocks at about 440.3 million lbs at the end of April, up from 404.7 million the previous month and 385.5 million a year ago.
However, beef stocks fell to 285.3 million lbs from 290.4 million last month and 335.6 million last year.
Total red meat supplies were put at 752.5 million lbs versus 748.6 million a year ago.

Pork belly supplies are the most watched part of the report, and most analysts look for CME pork belly futures to open 0.500 to 1.000 cent per lb higher on Wednesday following a decline in belly stocks during April.
"This is only the second time in history that we ever had a drawdown in stocks during the month of April," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst with Alaron Trading Corp.
USDA reported frozen belly stocks as of April 30 at 54.017 million lbs, down from March 31 stocks of 54.767 million lbs. Early estimates ranged from 52.2 to 59.0 million lbs on hand.
"This is the third smallest figure for that date in history, going back at least into the 1950s," Levitt said.
But not all analysts were bullish.

"If export demand was that good, that means domestic demand had to be pretty bad. Our kill was consistently four to six percent below a year ago, yet we only have three million lbs less in storage than a year ago," said Rich Tokheim from Investment Research Company.
"If the (futures) market opens higher, then I think it's going to trade lower at some time on the day," Tokheim said.
Total beef stocks showed high usage compared to the rate of production, or cattle slaughter, and was one of the few categories to show a month-on-month decline.
"When you look at what has happened in the last year with all the cow kill, and then we see the beef stocks decline, it makes (beef stocks) substantially friendly," Benson said.
However, the cattle futures market may not rally on the beef stocks as it is currently being influenced by the next expected direction in cash fed cattle markets, Benson added.
